text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Local flights paralysed by shortage of aviation fuel.
- Police warn students against staging any demonstrations on Thursday to mark the fourth anniversary of the annulled June 12, 1993 presidential election.
- Improved operating results raise share price of Nigerian Ropes Plc.
- Dissatisfied with banks preference for short-term lending that has starved priority sectors of funds, the central bank may re-introduce sectoral credit allocation system dumped last year.
- Lagos and Abuja still groan under fuel shortage as only few pump stations have petrol.
- Death toll in last Friday's oil tanker explosion in Lagos port rises to three as one of the injured crew men dies.
- Nigeria Airways reaches agreement with Cameroon Airline to fly its passengers to London following the ban by Britain and Nigeria on each other's planes.
- The management of Daily Times of Nigeria, the country's biggest newspaper group, is negotiating to recapitalise the company, says its sole administrator Peter Enahoro.
- Government has directed state electricity company NEPA to source locally for 18 components it needs in order to save on foreign exchange.
- The federal government may have set August as deadline for a technical committee to submit detailed schedule for privatisation of some public utilities.
